Microsoft Office/Microsoft Outlook
📧

Microsoft Outlook

Email, calendar, contacts and tasks the way a busy medical office uses them: writing professional messages, keeping a shared inbox under control, scheduling meetings across a team, and protecting patient information.

6+

Practice simulations

Which Outlook does this course teach?

This course teaches the new Outlook for Windows, which looks and works almost the same as Outlook on the web. The practice simulations are copies of the new Outlook window. Where classic Outlook (the desktop app with a File tab) works differently, the lesson tells you, so you can follow along on either one.

Certification: Microsoft does not offer an Outlook exam in its Microsoft 365 Apps series. The Microsoft Office Specialist Outlook exam that Certiport currently lists is Outlook Associate (Office 2019), exam MO-400, which is based on classic Outlook.

Course Modules

Work through the modules in order. Each module ends with practice in a working copy of Outlook.

Module 1
📧

Getting Started with Outlook

Which Outlook you are using, how the new Outlook window is laid out, and reading and managing messages.

Module 2
✍️

Writing Professional Email

Addressing and structuring messages, replying and forwarding, attachments and cloud links, signatures, and Schedule send, Undo send and recall.

Module 3
🗂️

Organizing Your Inbox

Folders and Favorites, categories, flags, pins and snooze, rules and Sweep, search and filters, quick steps and Focused Inbox.

Module 4
📅

Calendar and Meetings

Calendar views, events and reminders, answering invitations, the Scheduling Assistant, recurring and Teams meetings, calendar sharing, delegates and time zones.

Module 5
👥

People and To Do

Contacts and contact lists in People, and To Do with due dates, importance, My Day and the Flagged email list.

Module 6
🛡️

Working Smarter and Safely

Automatic replies, shared mailboxes, phishing and junk email, sensitivity labels, encryption and accessible messages, and Copilot and Outlook on other devices.

What You'll Need

  • • Nothing to install: every lesson has practice simulations you can do on a school computer
  • • Optional: the new Outlook for Windows, classic Outlook, or Outlook on the web with a work or school account
  • • Never practice with real patient information. Use the fictional Lakeside Medical Associates examples
